framing: Hardware and software as one experience, or two products taped together.

blocks.label: Intake
blocks.body: Watch Apple's Apple Watch Design Tips and Tricks. Ignore every word about WatchKit. What you are after is the argument for holistic design: the claim that the crown, the case, the tap on your wrist and the pixels are one product, and that a phone app shrunk down is a different, worse thing.
detail: Watch at 1.25x if you must, but do not skim the first third.
Write down every moment where a hardware decision forces a software decision, or the reverse.
Notice how often the answer to a design problem is a physical control rather than a screen.

blocks.label: Bench
blocks.body: Finish object one. Now go back through your three columns and mark each row: was this interaction chosen for this object, or inherited because that is how such things are done? Inherited is not an insult. It is a place someone stopped thinking.
detail: Chosen: someone argued about it, and the object would be worse the other way.
Inherited: it is a button because the last one had a button.
Expect roughly two chosen rows out of eight. That ratio is the whole point of the exercise.

blocks.label: Log
blocks.body: One line on what exists now that did not exist last night.

source.title: Apple Watch Design Tips and Tricks (WWDC15)

done_when: Object one card is complete and every row is marked chosen or inherited.
question: Which inherited interaction on your object would you defend anyway, and why?

object.name: Apple Watch Digital Crown
object.why: A hundred-year-old watch part repurposed as a scroll input, kept because your finger covers the screen and the screen is the size of a stamp.

note: Holistic design. Introduces chosen vs inherited, which runs all week and returns in week 2 as the basis for the modality swap.
